<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The requirements are now clear. I am designing the solution.

A shared `BlockOrderModel` will unify detection and fixing. Detection will populate the model. Fixing will reorder statements so logic and other code stay first while nested functions follow, topo-sorted. This handles the single-nested-function edge case. The spike recommends preserving relative order for logic and other code, then placing nested functions in caller-before-callee order.

The implementation plan is set. A new `src/nested-block-order.ts` module will hold the shared model, detection, and reordering logic. The detector will be rewired to consume it. Transform nested logic will move from the fixer into this module, leaving the fixer as a thin delegate.

Concrete file names are now set. `src/nested-block-order.ts` will hold the model, builder, detector, and reordering logic. Transform visitors will move to `src/nested-block-transform.ts`. The fixer will become a thin delegate. Convergence tests will be added.

Detection will iterate function bodies, build a BlockOrderModel for each, and map findings to NestedFunctionViolation. I noticed a subtle difference between the current `isReferencedInFunctionBody` logic and the spike's `referencedNested` collection: the current code searches the entire body including nested function bodies, while the spike likely excludes definitions. I need to verify this behavior before finalizing the detector.

I traced the current `isReferencedInFunctionBody` logic. It skips the local definition but recurses into other nested function bodies, so references inside those bodies count. The `referencedNested` set should therefore include names found in logic, other statements, and nested functions.

Detection will keep the current reference-scanning behavior, including references inside other nested function bodies. This preserves compatibility with the existing detector. During fixing, nested functions that are referenced will be skipped if moving them would break temporal dead zone rules.

I noticed the current fixer always moves nested functions to the end after other statements. This can break temporal dead zone rules for const and let bindings. However, function declarations are hoisted, so moving them does not affect runtime behavior. The fixer must still respect the referencedNested set to avoid breaking TDZ for variables.

The fixer will partition nested functions by reference status. Unreferenced nested functions will be reordered to the end after logic, topo-sorted. Referenced nested functions will remain in place to avoid breaking temporal dead zone rules.

I verified the lone unreferenced nested case. It correctly moves after logic.

I also checked the no-logic edge case. Without logic, detection returns early and the fixer leaves nested functions alone. The referencedNested set only scans logic and other statements, so nested references inside other nested bodies are excluded.

I confirmed the spike's `referencedNested` scope: only identifiers in logic and other statements, not inside nested function bodies. This keeps the describe pattern working correctly. I am now drafting the `buildBlockOrderModel` interface, defining statement kinds and a name field for nested functions.

The `BlockOrderModel` interface now includes statement nodes, start lines, nested dependency edges, and the `referencedNested` set. A `NestedFuncEdge` connects caller and callee names. Statements classify as `nestedFunc` when they are named declarations or variable statements containing function-like initializers. The existing single-arrow-per-statement extraction rule is preserved.

I resolved the classification ambiguity. All non-nested statements will be grouped as logic, since the spike only distinguishes logic from nested functions. The other category will remain empty for now. I am now drafting the detection logic from the model.

I finalized the detection and reorder algorithms. Detection uses the last logic statement line to decide whether to scan nested functions. Reorder pins referenced nested functions in place and topo-sorts only the unreferenced ones. I verified the lone-unreferenced-nested case and the no-logic case.

I verified the pinned-and-movable edge cases. A referenced nested function before logic stays fixed; otherwise unreferenced nested functions are topo-sorted after all logic. I also confirmed the transform must recurse into nested blocks. I am deciding between `nested-block-order.ts` and `nested-transform.ts` for the reorder logic.

I settled on a single `nested-block-order.ts` file for the model, detector, and reorder logic. The transform visitor will live in `nested-block-transform.ts`, imported by the fixer. I also verified that the reorder guard already allows lone nested functions when logic precedes them.

I refined the reorder guard. Instead of returning null for single-nested or logic-less bodies, I will always compute a new order and return null only when the result is identical to the original. I also need to remove a stale comment about VariableStatement.

The detector rewrite will keep visiting functions and building models per body, while still recursing into nested function bodies. The functionMap remains necessary for NestedFunctionViolation objects. The parentName field in the model may be unnecessary if detection infers parent from the visit context. I will check existing helpers for fixCode and analyzeCode patterns to structure the convergence tests.
</details></think>
